html:
In 1707 a succession quarrel split Lan Xang into the kingdoms of Luang Phrabang in the north and Vientiane in the centre; Champasak in the south broke away in 1713.

The three rival kingdoms each looked to stronger neighbours for help, and all fell under the power of Siam in 1779, when Siamese armies took Vientiane and carried off the Emerald Buddha.

Vientiane was destroyed after the revolt of Anouvong in 1827. The Luang Phrabang line survived, and under French rule its king became king of all Laos. The monarchy ended with the communist victory of 1975; see Kaysone Phomvihane.
